name: Vampire Lacerator
oracle_text: At the beginning of your upkeep, you lose 1 life unless an opponent has 10 or less life.
blocked_sentences: At the beginning of your upkeep, you lose 1 life unless an opponent has 10 or less life.

Scope: only the "unless an opponent has 10 or less life" clause is blocked. The `upkeep` trigger (`{"event": "upkeep", "controller": "you"}`, exactly as Phyrexian Arena writes it) and the `lose_life` half are both expressible today, so this card becomes writable the moment the quantifier below exists.

needs.what: per-player aggregate value expressions over a multi-player spec -- `min_life_of` / `max_life_of` (and the same shape for other player quantities such as cards in hand), so `{"min_life_of": "each_opponent"}` yields the life total of the opponent who has the least rather than a total across opponents. With that, "an opponent has 10 or less life" is `{"cmp": "<=", "left": {"min_life_of": "each_opponent"}, "right": {"const": 10}}`
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `life_of` is the only way to read a life total and it SUMS over its player spec (`values.py:104` does `sum(ctx.state.players[p].life for p in pids)`), and `"opponent"` is a plain alias for `"each_opponent"` -- `select_players` (`selectors.py:278-279`) returns `ctx.opponents()` for both. So `{"life_of": "opponent"} <= 10` reads as "my opponents' COMBINED life is 10 or less", which is identical to the printed card in a duel but diverges sharply in a pod: three opponents at 40 sum to 120, so the exemption becomes effectively unreachable and the card applies its own drawback in games where the real one would not. `min`/`max` exist as value expressions but take a list of value expressions, and there is no per-opponent player spec to feed them -- the player specs are `you`, `opponent`/`each_opponent`, `each_player`, `active_player`, `{target}`, `{controller_of}`, `{owner_of}`, `{binding}`, none of which enumerates opponents one at a time

needs.what: a quantifier over players in the condition DSL -- `{"any_player": {"players": "each_opponent", "condition": {...}}}` and its `each_player` counterpart -- evaluating the inner condition once per selected player and OR-ing (resp. AND-ing) the results, so "an opponent has 10 or less life" and "each opponent has 10 or less life" become distinguishable. This is the general form; the `min_life_of` value above is the narrow special case
needs.why_existing_wont_do: the condition DSL (`conditions.py`, CONDITION_KEYS = cmp/all/any/not/exists/zone_is/is_your_turn/kicked) has no player-scoped form at all. `all`/`any` combine a fixed literal list of sub-conditions written into the card, not a list generated per player, so they cannot range over an opponent count that is unknown until the game is set up. `exists` looks the closest but quantifies over OBJECTS -- it calls `resolve_pool` on an object selector -- and there is no player selector to hand it. `{"controller_of": "snapshot_name"}` does yield a single player, but it is whichever one arbitrary opponent happens to control the snapshotted permanent, and an opponent controlling nothing is invisible to it, so it cannot express "any opponent"
